name: context-watch
description: Tells the model its context size and plan usage at each 100k and usage mark, suggests a clear, logs it, lets it compact or clear itself and carry on, runs a night on to a line on the week meter, and holds a door at each new context for the background jobs still running; /context-watch shows and changes the settings

contextStep.title: Context step (tokens)
contextStep.description: A notice each time the context passes a multiple of this many tokens.

clearAt.title: Suggested clear (tokens)
clearAt.description: A notice when the context passes this many tokens: land the work in files, then clear. 0 turns it off. /context-watch epoch sets one for the current context only.

fiveHourMarks.title: 5-hour usage marks (%)
fiveHourMarks.description: Comma-separated percentages of the 5-hour usage window that raise a notice. Empty: none.

weeklyMarks.title: Weekly usage marks (%)
weeklyMarks.description: Comma-separated percentages of the weekly usage window that raise a notice. Empty: none.

statusLine.title: Status line
statusLine.description: Show the context size and usage in the status line after each tool call.

dataDir.title: Data folder
dataDir.description: Where the log and the per-project files of last turns go. A leading ~ is your home folder.

log.title: Log
log.description: Append each crossing, compaction and clear to context-watch.log in the data folder.

logMaxBytes.title: Log size cap (bytes)
logMaxBytes.description: Past this size the log keeps its newer half.

keepTurns.title: Turns kept per project
keepTurns.description: How many of the last turns' words are kept per project, to show again after a /clear. 0 turns this off.

resumeNote.title: Resume note
resumeNote.description: Text put into every prompt that resumes the work after the mod's compaction or clear, before the model's own brief: say, what to read first in every project. Empty: none.

door.title: The door at each new context
door.description: Log each background job (Bash run in the background, Monitor) and hold a clear or compaction, and the first tool calls after the user's /clear, until every job still running is carried on (named in the next context, with why) or stopped. The Mac's load shows at the door and at each context mark.
